actions.cancel_query.description: Cancel a running query by its query ID.

actions.count_rows.description: Count the rows of a table that match optional filters.
actions.count_rows.props.filters.descrip: Conditions combined with AND. Each has a column, an operator (=, !=, <, <=, >, >=, IN, NOT IN, LIKE, ILIKE, IS NULL, IS NOT NULL) and a value. For IN / NOT IN pass a list or comma-separated values; IS NULL / IS NOT NULL take no value.

actions.create_dynamic_table.description: Create or replace a Snowflake Dynamic Table that automatically refreshes based on a query. Dynamic Tables are a declarative way to define a table whose content is derived from a query, updated on a schedule.
actions.create_dynamic_table.props.datab: Select the Snowflake database to use. Databases are listed under **Data → Databases** in the Snowflake console.
actions.create_dynamic_table.props.query: The SELECT statement that defines the content of the dynamic table. Example: `SELECT user_id, SUM(amount) AS total FROM orders GROUP BY user_id`
actions.create_dynamic_table.props.schem: Select the schema within the chosen database. Schemas are listed under **Data → Databases → [your database]** in the Snowflake console.
actions.create_dynamic_table.props.table: The name for the new dynamic table (e.g. `DAILY_SALES_SUMMARY`). Only letters, digits, underscores, and `$` are allowed.
actions.create_dynamic_table.props.targe: How up-to-date the dynamic table data should be (called **Target Lag** in Snowflake). Examples: `1 minute`, `5 minutes`, `1 hour`. Use `DOWNSTREAM` to only refresh when a downstream object explicitly requests it.
actions.create_dynamic_table.props.wareh: Select the virtual warehouse to use for this operation. Warehouses are listed under **Admin → Warehouses** in the Snowflake console. Leave empty to use the warehouse set in your connection.
actions.delete_row.description: Delete one or more rows from a Snowflake table that match a WHERE condition.

actions.delete_row.props.schema.descript: Select the schema within the chosen database. Schemas are listed under **Data → Databases → [your database]** in the Snowflake console.

Only use static values or data from trusted, internal steps — never pass unvalidated end-user input here.
actions.delete_row_by_key.description: Delete the one row whose key column equals a value.

actions.delete_row_by_key.props.table.de: Table name, optionally qualified as DATABASE.SCHEMA.TABLE (e.g. `ANALYTICS.PUBLIC.ORDERS`). An unqualified name uses the connection default database and schema. Unquoted names are case-insensitive; wrap a name in double quotes for exact case.
actions.delete_rows_by_filter.descriptio: Delete every row that matches the filters, up to a safety limit.
actions.delete_rows_by_filter.props.filt: Conditions combined with AND. Each has a column, an operator (=, !=, <, <=, >, >=, IN, NOT IN, LIKE, ILIKE, IS NULL, IS NOT NULL) and a value. For IN / NOT IN pass a list or comma-separated values; IS NULL / IS NOT NULL take no value. At least one filter is required.
actions.delete_rows_by_filter.props.maxR: Refuse (and roll back) if more rows than this would be deleted (1–10000). Defaults to 100.
actions.delete_rows_by_filter.props.tabl: Table name, optionally qualified as DATABASE.SCHEMA.TABLE (e.g. `ANALYTICS.PUBLIC.ORDERS`). An unqualified name uses the connection default database and schema. Unquoted names are case-insensitive; wrap a name in double quotes for exact case.

actions.list_columns.props.limit.descrip: Maximum number of items to return (1–1000). Defaults to 200.

actions.load_data_from_stage.description: Load data into a Snowflake table from a named internal or external stage using COPY INTO.
actions.load_data_from_stage.props.datab: Select the Snowflake database to use. Databases are listed under **Data → Databases** in the Snowflake console.
actions.load_data_from_stage.props.error: When enabled, the load fails if the number of columns in a file does not match the number of columns in the target table. Disable to allow files with fewer columns. Only applies to CSV files.
actions.load_data_from_stage.props.file_: The file format of the data files in the stage.

Optional regular expression to load only files whose names match the pattern (e.g. `.*\.csv` loads only `.csv` files, `sales_2024.*` loads files that start with `sales_2024`). Leave empty to load all files in the stage path.
actions.load_data_from_stage.props.on_er: What to do when a row fails validation during loading.
actions.load_data_from_stage.props.schem: Select the schema within the chosen database. Schemas are listed under **Data → Databases → [your database]** in the Snowflake console.
actions.load_data_from_stage.props.skip_: Number of rows to skip at the top of each CSV file (e.g. `1` to skip a column-header row). Only applies to CSV files. Defaults to 0.
actions.load_data_from_stage.props.stage: Path to the Snowflake stage (a staging area that holds files before loading). For **internal stages**: use `@stage_name` or `@schema.stage_name/folder/`. For **external stages** (S3, GCS, Azure): use `@schema.stage_name/prefix/`. Example: `@my_stage/data/`. You can find your stage names under **Data → Databases → [your database] → Stages**.
actions.load_data_from_stage.props.table: Select the table to work with.
actions.runMultipleQueries.description: Execute multiple SQL statements in sequence against your Snowflake database. Optionally wrap them in a transaction so all changes are rolled back if any statement fails.
actions.runMultipleQueries.props.applica: An optional label sent to Snowflake to identify this client. Visible in query history under **Monitoring → Query History → Client Application**.
actions.runMultipleQueries.props.binds.d: Values shared across all queries for the numbered placeholders (`:1`, `:2`…). Provide them in order. Unused parameters are allowed.
actions.runMultipleQueries.props.sqlText: List of SQL statements to run in order. Use `:1`, `:2`… placeholders to reference shared **Parameters** values. Avoid `?` placeholders when running multiple queries — use numbered placeholders instead to prevent unexpected behaviour.
actions.runMultipleQueries.props.timeout: Maximum time in milliseconds each query may run before Snowflake cancels it (applied as STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_IN_SECONDS, capped at 540 seconds). Defaults to 30 000 ms (30 seconds).
actions.runMultipleQueries.props.useTran: When enabled, all queries run inside a single transaction. If any query fails, every preceding change in this batch is rolled back automatically.
actions.runQuery.description: Execute a SQL query against your Snowflake database and return the results as rows.
actions.runQuery.props.application.descr: An optional label sent to Snowflake to identify this client. Visible in query history under **Monitoring → Query History → Client Application**. Useful for auditing which automation triggered a query.
actions.runQuery.props.binds.description: Values to bind to the placeholders (`:1`, `:2`…, or `?`) in the SQL query. Provide them in the same order they appear in the query. Using parameters is the safe way to pass dynamic values — never concatenate user input directly into the SQL.
actions.runQuery.props.sqlText.descripti: The SQL statement to execute. Use `:1`, `:2`… or `?` as placeholders for the **Parameters** values below to safely pass dynamic values without SQL injection risk.
actions.runQuery.props.timeout.descripti: Maximum time in milliseconds the query may run before Snowflake cancels it (applied as STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_IN_SECONDS, capped at 540 seconds). Defaults to 30 000 ms (30 seconds).
actions.run_select_query.description: Run one read-only SQL query (SELECT, WITH, SHOW, DESCRIBE or EXPLAIN).
actions.run_select_query.props.limit.des: Maximum number of items to return (1–1000). Defaults to 100.
actions.run_select_query.props.parameter: Values for the ? placeholders, in order.
actions.run_select_query.props.sql.descr: One read-only statement, e.g. `SELECT ID, EMAIL FROM ANALYTICS.PUBLIC.USERS WHERE CREATED_AT > ?`. Use ? placeholders for values.
actions.search_rows.description: Search for rows in a Snowflake table using an optional WHERE condition, ordering, and row limit.

actions.search_rows.props.limit.descript: Maximum number of rows to return (1–10 000). Defaults to 100.
actions.search_rows.props.order_by.descr: Optional column(s) to sort results by (SQL ORDER BY clause). Only use static values or data from trusted, internal steps — never pass unvalidated end-user input here.
actions.search_rows.props.schema.descrip: Select the schema within the chosen database. Schemas are listed under **Data → Databases → [your database]** in the Snowflake console.
actions.search_rows.props.table.descript: Select the table to work with.
actions.search_rows.props.where_clause.d: Optional SQL WHERE condition to narrow down results (e.g. `status = 'active' AND age > 18`). Only use static values or data from trusted, internal steps — never pass unvalidated end-user input here.
actions.update_row.description: Update one or more rows in a Snowflake table that match a WHERE condition.

actions.update_row_by_key.props.values.d: Column names mapped to new values, e.g. {"STATUS": "shipped"}.
actions.update_rows_by_filter.descriptio: Update every row that matches the filters, up to a safety limit.

actions.update_rows_by_filter.props.maxR: Refuse (and roll back) if more rows than this would be updated (1–10000). Defaults to 100.
actions.update_rows_by_filter.props.tabl: Table name, optionally qualified as DATABASE.SCHEMA.TABLE (e.g. `ANALYTICS.PUBLIC.ORDERS`). An unqualified name uses the connection default database and schema. Unquoted names are case-insensitive; wrap a name in double quotes for exact case.
actions.update_rows_by_filter.props.valu: Column names mapped to new values, e.g. {"STATUS": "archived"}.
